key_insight: Capping CsPbBr3 thin films with few-layer hBN dramatically improves heat dissipation without changing the perovskite’s morphology or optical properties.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to more thermally robust perovskite optoelectronic devices, especially under high excitation or continuous-wave operation.
method: Large-scale semidry transfer of few-layer hBN onto planar hot-pressed CsPbBr3 thin films
Microscopic and spectroscopic checks to verify preserved film morphology and optical response
Heat diffusion simulations to compare thermal transport in capped vs. bare films
evidence_signal: The hBN-capped heterostructure reached an estimated thermal conductivity of 3 W/(m·K), about 7× higher than the 0.45 W/(m·K) bare CsPbBr3 film, and showed reduced laser-induced heating under high-power CW excitation.
watch_item: Scaling this approach into full devices will still require careful control of interface quality, transfer uniformity, and long-term stability under operating conditions.
paper_title: Improved Heat Dissipation in CsPbBr${_3}$-hBN Heterostructures
